card.occupation: Chartered civil engineer specialising in drainage and flood risk, working for a mid-sized engineering consultancy. He splits his time between the Maidstone office, working from home two days a week, and site visits around Kent and East Sussex.
card.education_detail: Went to a comprehensive in Tonbridge and did A-levels in Maths, Physics and Geography. Took a BEng in Civil Engineering at the University of Nottingham, then became chartered (CEng, ICE) at 29 through his employer's training scheme.
card.household: Lives with his partner of eleven years, Claire, a primary school deputy head, and their son Alfie, who is 9. They have a three-bed semi on the edge of town with a long, slightly neglected garden. They've never married. Neither of them felt strongly about it, and the money went on the house deposit instead. There's also an elderly cat called Biscuit, which came with Claire.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in west Kent to a dad who was a quantity surveyor and a mum who worked in a building society. He was christened Church of England and went to Cubs at the church hall. He still calls himself Christian and goes to the parish church at Christmas, Easter and for Alfie's school services, but he isn't a regular. Fairly typical middle-England upbringing: caravan holidays, Sunday roasts, Saturday football on the radio.
card.professional_persona: Steady and practical, and good in a crisis. He's the person who gets sent to the site when a culvert's collapsed or a client is panicking about a planning objection, because he doesn't get rattled. He manages a small team of three graduates and is fair but not especially chatty with them. He's thorough enough on the technical side, a bit last-minute with timesheets, and dislikes long internal meetings.
card.sports_persona: Supports Charlton Athletic out of habit from his dad and goes to The Valley three or four times a season. He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with a group from work and their mates, and is described by others as 'surprisingly competitive for someone so laid-back'. He does the occasional parkrun if Claire drags him, and watches the cricket on TV in summer.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person. He listens to a lot of podcasts, mostly history and true-crime-lite, and likes Britpop and older indie such as Blur, Supergrass and Elbow. He'll watch a decent crime drama with Claire and has a soft spot for documentaries about engineering disasters. He's been to the theatre a handful of times, usually for birthdays.
card.travel_persona: Prefers a self-catering holiday where he can do some walking and cook on a barbecue: the Lake District, Cornwall, once the Dordogne. Every couple of years they do a week somewhere warm with a pool for Alfie, usually Portugal or Crete. He's unbothered by flying, delays or lost luggage, which Claire finds both reassuring and annoying.
card.culinary_persona: He does most of the weekend cooking: a roast on Sunday, a big chilli or curry from scratch on Saturday. Weekday dinners are whoever gets in first. He has a decent barbecue he's quite proud of. He drinks real ale, mainly local Kentish stuff from Shepherd Neame, and the odd glass of red. He isn't fussy and will eat anything.
hobbies_and_interests: Going to Charlton games with his dad
Walking on the North Downs Way
Slowly fixing up the garden shed
Helping coach Alfie's under-10s football on Saturday mornings
skills: Staying calm and making decisions under pressure
Explaining technical problems to non-technical clients
Basic DIY: plumbing, tiling, putting up shelves
card.career_goals: He would like to make associate director in the next few years, mostly for the pay and the chance to pick his projects. He has no burning ambition beyond that. He'd consider going independent as a flood risk consultant in his fifties if the work was there. He wants to keep the working-from-home days whatever happens.
card.voice: Relaxed, mid-pace, standard south-eastern English with a slight Kent/estuary edge: some glottal stops ('bi' of a problem'), 'yeah' as a starter, and the occasional 'mate' when he's warmed up. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal. He uses 'er' rather than 'erm' when thinking and leans on 'sort of' as a hedge ('it's sort of my area'). He'll add 'you know' or 'yeah' at the end of a point. Silence doesn't bother him at all. He's happy to sit and think, and might just say 'hang on, let me think about that' and actually do it. He gives straightforward answers without much embellishment and sometimes undersells things.
card.typing: Quick and functional. He mostly starts with a capital letter and uses full stops but often skips the final one. Apostrophes are usually there but sometimes dropped in a hurry ('dont'). Very few abbreviations beyond 'etc' and the odd 'tbh'. Short sentences, no emojis. He'll answer the question asked and not much more, e.g. 'Mostly drive to work, train if im going into London. Its about 25 mins'
card.with_strangers: Easy-going and polite without being overly warm. He comes across as unflappable and a bit dry. He doesn't fill gaps with chatter but will happily talk once someone asks him about something he knows. Some people read his calmness as slightly detached. He isn't nervous on calls and doesn't apologise much, except a quick 'sorry, say that again?' if the audio cuts out.
small_things: The A20 roadworks that have been going on forever
Charlton's latest result and how 'it's always the hope that kills you'
What he cooked at the weekend
Alfie's football team losing 7–1 and nobody minding
The cat being sick on the stairs again
Needing to sort out the guttering before winter
A podcast episode about the Tay Bridge disaster
deeper_things: His dad had a stroke two years ago. He handled the hospital, the care plans and the forms practically and calmly, and only later realised he'd never really talked to anyone about how he felt about it
Claire sometimes says he's hard to read, and he's aware it can come across as not caring when he just doesn't worry much
He's privately fine with never getting married, but knows his mum would still love them to
He wonders now and then whether he settled into engineering a bit by default rather than choosing it
He's not sure what he believes religiously, but likes the church at Christmas and finds it steadying
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam set slightly below eye level, so the angle looks a little up at him. Daylight comes from a window off to the left, lighting that side of his face more brightly, with a ceiling light on as well. He's a white man in his early forties with short, mid-brown hair, slightly receding at the temples and greying at the sides, and a day or two of stubble. His expression is neutral and relaxed, with a faint half-smile and his eyes looking just past the camera at the screen. No glasses. He's wearing a navy quarter-zip fleet-style jumper over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a small box-room home office: a white wall with a framed print of an Ordnance Survey map of the Medway area, a cheap IKEA shelf holding lever-arch files labelled with project numbers, a Charlton Athletic mug, and a hard hat and hi-vis vest hooked on the back of the door, which is partly open to the landing.
